Implementation and tests clearly exist and align with the story requirements:
1. Rules implemented - `src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts` - Declares ESLint rule module `require-story-annotation`. - Uses shared helpers and visitor builder: - `import { buildVisitors } from "./helpers/require-story-visitors";` - `import { DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode } from "./helpers/require-story-helpers";` - Meta/schema: - `fixable: "code"` (auto-fix support for @story, which is actually beyond 003.0 but compatible). - `messages.missingStory` provides clear, actionable text: "Function '{{name}}' must have an explicit @story annotation...". - Schema exposes options: `scope` (array, enum = DEFAULT_SCOPE) and `exportPriority` ("all" | "exported" | "non-exported"). - `create(context)` wires options, passes `shouldProcessNode` and options into `buildVisitors`. - File is explicitly annotated with the story: - `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` - `@req REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED`.
- `src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts` - Declares ESLint rule module `require-req-annotation`. - Imports shared scope/export logic and @req-specific checker: - `import { DEFAULT_SCOPE, EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES, shouldProcessNode } from "./helpers/require-story-helpers";` - `import { checkReqAnnotation } from "../utils/annotation-checker";` - Options type includes `scope` and `exportPriority`, mirroring `require-story-annotation`. - Meta/schema: - `fixable: "code"` (though this rule currently calls `checkReqAnnotation` with `{ enableFix: false }`, so no fixes are actually applied yet; allowed for this story). - `messages.missingReq` clearly tells user to add a `@req` annotation and gives an example. - Schema for `scope` and `exportPriority` matches the story rule and documentation. - `create(context)`: - Derives `scope` from options (defaults to `DEFAULT_SCOPE`). - Derives `exportPriority` (default `"all"`). - Constructs `shouldCheck` using shared `shouldProcessNode`. - Defines visitors for: - `FunctionDeclaration` - `FunctionExpression` (skips when parent is `MethodDefinition`) - `MethodDefinition` - `TSDeclareFunction` - `TSMethodSignature` - Each visitor calls `runCheck(node)` which defers to `checkReqAnnotation` when `shouldCheck(node)` is true. - File annotated for this story: - `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md` - `@req REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION`, `REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT`, `REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`, `REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY`.
2. Shared detection, scope, and export-priority behavior - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-core.ts` - Defines `DEFAULT_SCOPE`: - `"FunctionDeclaration"`, `"FunctionExpression"`, `"MethodDefinition"`, `"TSMethodSignature"`, `"TSDeclareFunction"`. - Arrow functions are NOT included, matching **REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION** (and explicitly excluding arrows by default). - `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES = ["all", "exported", "non-exported"]`. - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts` - Re-exports `DEFAULT_SCOPE` and `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES` and defines: - `isExportedNode(node)` that walks up parent chain and detects `ExportNamedDeclaration` / `ExportDefaultDeclaration`. - `shouldProcessNode(node, scope, exportPriority)`: - Returns false if `node.type` not in `scope`. - Uses `isExportedNode` and `exportPriority` ("all" / "exported" / "non-exported") to determine if node is in scope. - These helpers are used by BOTH rules (`require-story-annotation` and `require-req-annotation`) to enforce **REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE** and **REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY** consistently.
3. Function-like construct coverage (REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION & REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT) - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-visitors.ts` for `require-story-annotation`: - Builds visitors for: - `FunctionDeclaration` → `handleFunctionDeclaration` - `FunctionExpression` (skipping when parent is `MethodDefinition`) - `ArrowFunctionExpression` (but gated by `options.shouldProcessNode`, which checks `scope`; since `DEFAULT_SCOPE` excludes arrows and `schema` enum does not include arrows, arrow functions are effectively excluded from enforcement by default, satisfying "arrow functions are excluded by default"). - `TSDeclareFunction` - `TSMethodSignature` - `MethodDefinition` - `src/rules/require-req-annotation.ts` visitors: - `FunctionDeclaration`, `FunctionExpression` (with method skip), `MethodDefinition`, `TSDeclareFunction`, `TSMethodSignature`. - Thus, in practice, BOTH rules enforce annotations on the same function-like constructs: - `FunctionDeclaration` - `FunctionExpression` (non-method) - `MethodDefinition` - `TSDeclareFunction` - `TSMethodSignature` - Arrow functions are not enforced because their type is not in `DEFAULT_SCOPE` and not permitted by the schema, matching the requirement that they are excluded by default.
4. JSDoc and annotation parsing (REQ-JSDOC-PARSING & error handling) - For `@story`: - `src/rules/helpers/require-story-helpers.ts`: - `jsdocHasStory(sourceCode, node)` uses `sourceCode.getJSDocComment(node)` and checks for `"@story"`. - `commentsBeforeHasStory(sourceCode, node)` uses `sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node)` and scans for `"@story"`. - `leadingCommentsHasStory(node)` inspects `node.leadingComments`. - `linesBeforeHasStory`, `parentChainHasStory`, `fallbackTextBeforeHasStory` are imported from `require-story-io` and use bounded line/character windows with guards and `try/catch` for malformed locations or missing APIs. - `hasStoryAnnotation(sourceCode, node)` composes all these in a `try { ... } catch { /* noop */ }` block to avoid crashes on malformed JSDoc/comments, satisfying **Error Handling** acceptance. - For `@req`: - `src/utils/annotation-checker.ts` mirrors the above strategy: - Uses `getJSDocComment`, `getCommentsBefore`, `getLeadingComments`, and `combineComments`. - Reuses constants `LOOKBACK_LINES` and `FALLBACK_WINDOW` from `require-story-io`, ensuring a shared heuristic window with the story rule. - `linesBeforeHasReq`, `parentChainHasReq`, `fallbackTextBeforeHasReq` implement line-based, parent-chain, and fallback text window scanning for `"@req"`, with extensive guards and `try/catch` to fail gracefully. - `hasReqAnnotation(jsdoc, comments, context, node)` prefers the heuristic checks when `sourceCode` and `node` are available, then falls back to raw JSDoc/comments scanning. All wrapped in `try/catch` for robustness. - `checkReqAnnotation(context, node, options)` pulls all this together and reports via `reportMissing` only when no `@req` is found. - This satisfies **REQ-JSDOC-PARSING** and the acceptance criterion for robust error handling of malformed comments and edge cases.
5. Error reporting & location (REQ-ERROR-LOCATION and UX) - `require-story-annotation`: - `reportMissing(context, sourceCode, node, passedTarget?)` in `require-story-helpers`: - Derives `functionName` from `extractName` which walks `node` and its parents, handling identifiers, keys, literals, and computed keys. - Chooses `nameNode` as: - `node.id` if identifier, - else `node.key` if identifier, - else `node`. - Calls `context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingStory", data: { name, functionName: name }, ... })`. - This means for named declarations and methods, errors are anchored on the function/method name; for anonymous constructs, the closest meaningful AST node is used. - `reportMethod` similarly anchors on `node.key` when identifier, explicitly satisfying the method error location requirement. - `require-req-annotation`: - `reportMissing(context, node, enableFix)` in `annotation-checker.ts`: - Uses `getNodeName(node)` (from `require-story-utils.ts`) which supports many node shapes (identifiers, literals, member expressions, TS-specific nodes, JSX, etc.). - Chooses `nameNode` as `node.id` (Identifier) → `node.key` (Identifier) → `node`, providing best-effort location at the function/method name. - Calls `context.report({ node: nameNode, messageId: "missingReq", data: { name, functionName: name } })`. - Tests in `tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts` assert `data: { name: "...", functionName: "..." }` for many different node types, demonstrating that name resolution is consistent and specific. - Error messages are clear and actionable: - Story rule: "Function '{{name}}' must have an explicit @story annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @story ...". - Req rule: "Function '{{functionName}}' is missing a required @req annotation. Add a JSDoc or line comment with @req (for example, '@req REQ-EXAMPLE') ...". - This satisfies **User Experience** and **REQ-ERROR-LOCATION**.

Documentation (rule docs with examples and options) - `docs/rules/require-story-annotation.md`: - References this story: `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - Describes supported node types exactly as in **REQ-FUNCTION-DETECTION**. - Documents `scope` and `exportPriority` options, including enums and defaults. - Provides correct and incorrect examples, including TypeScript-specific forms (`TSDeclareFunction`, `TSMethodSignature`). - `docs/rules/require-req-annotation.md`: - References this story and **REQ-ANNOTATION-REQUIRED**. - Documents node coverage: function declarations, function expressions, method definitions, `TSDeclareFunction`, `TSMethodSignature`. - Explicitly notes that arrow functions are not checked and may be added later, aligning with story requirements. - Documents `scope` and `exportPriority` options, mirroring `require-story-annotation`. - Provides multiple correct/incorrect examples, including JS and TS syntax. - This fulfills the **Documentation** acceptance criterion.
7. Tests and RuleTester coverage - Story rule tests: `tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts` - Header explicitly references the story: - `@story docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`. - Uses `RuleTester` with JS parser by default and with `@typescript-eslint/parser` for TS cases. - Valid cases include: - JS function with JSDoc `@story`. - Line comment `// @story ...` before function. - FunctionExpression, arrow function, class method with `@story`. - TS `declare function` and TS `interface` method with `@story`. - Unannotated arrow function allowed by default (verifying arrow-exclusion semantics). - Invalid cases cover missing `@story` annotations for: - `FunctionDeclaration` (with expected auto-fix output and suggestion text). - `FunctionExpression` (variable-initializer style). - `MethodDefinition`. - `TSDeclareFunction`. - `TSMethodSignature`. - Additional suites verify configuration: - `exportPriority: "exported"` where unexported functions without `@story` are allowed, exported without `@story` are errors. - `scope: ["FunctionDeclaration"]` where only declarations are enforced and arrow functions are ignored.
- Req rule tests: `tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts` - Header also references this story and error-reporting story. - Uses `RuleTester` with JS parser and `@typescript-eslint/parser` for TS cases. - Valid cases include: - Functions with only `@req`. - Functions with both `@story` and `@req`. - TS `TSDeclareFunction` and `TSMethodSignature` with `@req`. - FunctionExpression, MethodDefinition, and TS function expressions as variable initializers (JS & TS) with `@req`. - Scope and exportPriority configurations where nodes are correctly ignored or required. - Invalid cases cover missing `@req` for: - Plain functions (with and without `@story`). - TS `declare function` and `TSMethodSignature`. - FunctionExpression (assigned to variable) and anonymous IIFEs. - MethodDefinition in class and object literal. - Multiple combinations of `scope` and `exportPriority` for functions and methods. - All invalid cases assert `messageId: "missingReq"` and `data: { name: ..., functionName: ... }`, verifying consistent error data.

Test execution evidence - `package.json` defines: - `"test": "jest --ci --bail"`. - Tests were executed via the prescribed command with verbose configuration: - Tool invocation: `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose`. - Reported command: `> jest --ci --bail --runInBand --verbose`. - No failures or error output were returned by the test run tool, indicating Jest exited successfully and all tests (including `tests/rules/require-story-annotation.test.ts` and `tests/rules/require-req-annotation.test.ts`) passed.
9. Cross-story integration and TypeScript support - Both rules and helpers explicitly import and support TS constructs: - `TSDeclareFunction` and `TSMethodSignature` visitors and checks implemented for both rules. - Tests use `@typescript-eslint/parser` to validate TS support. - Both rules share the same configuration semantics via `DEFAULT_SCOPE`, `EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES`, and `shouldProcessNode`, satisfying **REQ-TYPESCRIPT-SUPPORT**, **REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE**, and **REQ-EXPORT-PRIORITY**.
Overall, the implemented rules, helpers, documentation, and comprehensive RuleTester test suites collectively satisfy all the acceptance criteria and specific requirements of docs/stories/003.0-DEV-FUNCTION-ANNOTATIONS.story.md.
